newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close slightly lower, banks up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close slightly lower, banks up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged to a slightly lower close on Monday, the first trading day in the Chinese Lunar New Year of the Ox.
But brokers said the index would have been harder hit without the strength in finance counters, in particular HSBC Holdings.
"A large part of this (activity today) is Hongkong Bank," said David Williamson, director at W.I. Carr.
The Hang Seng Index slipped 16.96 points to close at 13,643.54, well off the day's opening high of 13,860.88. Turnover rose to HK$7.63 billion, compared with HK$7.25 billion last Wednesday.
The market surged 196 points at the open on a burst of speculative trading, hoping to ride on the back of positive new year sentiment. But the index slipped back steadily throughout the morning.

Finance counters, chiefly HSBC Holdings, led the market. The international banking giant closed HK$5.50 higher at HK$189.50, after setting an all time high of HK$191.50. Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.25 to HK$93.50.
Brokers said HSBC's gains were due in part to the strength of the U.S. dollar, which would boost the bank's earnings report in sterling.
"The bank's results will be out on March 3, and I expect the share to be strong in advance of that," said Robin Fox of Nomura Research Institute.
Williamson added he expected to see HSBC break through HK$200.00 per share.
"What we saw today was a negative, single-day reversal," said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Asia Securities.
The market opened high, but lacked momentum or real buying interest on the follow through and this was despite Wall Street's bullish performance on Friday, added To.
The Dow put on 82.74 points to 6,855.80, due chiefly to a favourable U.S. unemployment reports for January.
"This (intra-day) reversal is not very bearish, but it does further confirm technical resistance at 13,800 -14,000," said To.
Brokers also said they were concerned about the trend in the Hang Seng futures, where the spot month had been trading on average at a discount to the cash market since Christmas.
The Hang Seng Index futures contract for February closed 60 points lower at 13,560, an 83-point discount to the cash market. March closed 45 points down at 13,580.
The property sector was the worst performing. Sun Hung Kai Properties slipped HK$2.00 to HK$91.00 and Henderson Land eased HK$2.00 to HK$71.75.
Cheung Kong lost HK$1.50 to HK$74.25 on relatively large turnover of HK$298.73 million.
